items.title: Should Investors Chase LMT Stock After Its 15.5% Three-Month Gain?
items.summary: Lockheed Martin climbs 15.5% in three months as a record backlog, major missile defense contracts and expanding production reinforce its long-term growth outlook.

items.title: Lockheed Martin is Down 8% in 6 Months: Wall Street Pro Expects 30% Growth Within a Year
items.summary: Lockheed Martin just delivered a blowout quarter with a record-breaking backlog, yet the stock sits near a six-month low while one Wall Street analyst sees nearly 30% upside. The real question is whether a single ugly quarter buried a defense giant or exposed something deeper.

items.title: Boeing's Finished Flight Test Counts Most For A Different Jet
items.summary: Monday's approval was already telegraphed, the rare double upgrade beside it was not, and the finished flight test frees engineering capacity for a different program entirely.

items.title: This ETF, The IBD Stock Of The Day, Breaks Out As Cybersecurity Stocks Rebound
items.summary: Cybersecurity stocks have shrugged off AI fears. The Amplify Cybersecurity ETF is a diversified way to play the sector.

items.title: The Production Ramp That Could Repower Boeing Stock
items.summary: Boeing is delivering airplanes at a pace it has not managed in years, and almost none of the profit those airplanes will carry has shown up yet.

items.title: This Is the Most Attractive Defense Stock Right Now
items.summary: Recent declines have left several stocks looking attractive, according to Wall Street. But one large defense contractor looks better than the others right now.

items.title: GD Q2 Deep Dive: Aerospace and Shipyard Strength Drive Backlog to New Highs
items.summary: Aerospace and defense company General Dynamics (NYSE:GD) reported Q2 CY2026 results beating Wall Street’s revenue expectations, with sales up 8.1% year on year to $14.09 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $4.24 per share was 6.6% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

items.title: U.S. and allies display growing naval cooperation in Pacific drills
items.summary: Investing.com -- The U.S. and its allies conducted their largest Rim of the Pacific maritime exercise to date, demonstrating deepening military cooperation amid concerns about China and North Korea, the Wall Street Journal reported.
